scientific_card_excerpt.text: For a bounded connected C^{1,beta} filled conductor in R^3 (0<beta<1), let alpha be its free-space static SI polarizability, alpha=epsilon0 M, and fill only electrically shielded closed cavities. The source imports the PEC endpoint Hashin–Shtrikman inverse-trace inequality V Tr(M^(-1))<=1, citing Colbrook–Sadeghi arXiv:2608.20466v1 Theorem 4.2. Cauchy–Schwarz then gives Tr(alpha)>=9 epsilon0 V. With one known homogeneous material, m=rho(1-phi)V and R=Tr(alpha)/m, it derives R>=9 epsilon0/[rho(1-phi)]. An actually covered upper measurement bound R_U yields phi<=1-9 epsilon0/(rho R_U), independent of exterior shape within the admitted class. Large response returns UNKNOWN, not a porosity diagnosis. This is neither an open-pore bound nor a printed-part-integrity guarantee.
